# Apply Step 4: Opt and Verification

After a passing full-change Review, delegate an initial read-only inspection to a clean-context Optimizer. Assess its findings against the project goals, constraints, expected benefits, costs and risks. Authorize a group of worthwhile improvements or stop with reasons; you need not identify specific edits before requesting inspection.

After each implementation delivery, inspect the actual changes and verification evidence. Decide whether to continue with the current Optimizer, request a fresh-context inspection to reconsider potential opportunities, or stop. Keep further work within an explicit scope and use actual progress and expected value to guide continuation.

Before Seal, obtain independent Review for all retained changes not yet reviewed. Choose full-change or incremental Review according to the cumulative changes and their impact; risk determines the scope, not whether Review occurs. You may review earlier when useful. Further changes require renewed Review of those changes and their impact.

Record actual Opt deliveries, including inspections that produce no changes. Use `not_performed` only when Opt did not run. Preserve findings and reasons when you decline an identified opportunity. The Optimizer’s verification does not replace independent Review.

Supply mode=inspection for read-only discovery; mode=implementation authorizes one related group and its constraints. The Optimizer reports opportunities outside that group without implementing them. Do not automatically pass stageRules.apply to internal roles; pass task-relevant project constraints. You need not request a fresh inspection every batch or prove there are no further opportunities. Stop repetition without new evidence or substantive progress.

Check and commit retained changes after each implementation delivery, then record actual baseCommit/resultCommit with the current revision. You own result commits; the Optimizer does not create Git history. If no changes are retained, reuse the original commit; do not create an empty commit. Equal commits describe unchanged delivery state, not proof of a read-only process; report attempts and complete reversals honestly. Different commits create a Review obligation even if a change reverted earlier work. A no-change delivery does not erase earlier unreviewed changes.

Run the required tests and inspect actual results before Review; assess cumulative changes, dependencies and evidence when choosing the test and Review scope. Full tests are not automatic, but retained unreviewed changes cannot skip independent Review. Repair confirmed pre-existing Change defects and require supplemental Review of the repair and impact; it does not automatically replace full-change/incremental Review of all retained optimization changes. Never treat a confirmed defect as optional abandonment.

Repair or reverse optional regressions locally, verify recovery and retain reliable work. Follow .xirang/references/xirang-quality-recovery.md after interruption; .xirang/references/xirang-optimization-failure-diagnosis.md is optional diagnostic guidance. Preserve history, unresolved findings and honest test evidence.

Read .xirang/references/xirang-quality-cli.md for schemas and diagnostics. CLI-assigned recordedRevision and commit ancestry link later Review to the last change-producing delivery; CLI does not evaluate prose quality or run tests. When implementation and required verification are complete, continue to Step 5. Do not invoke retired delegation, verification, conclusion or checkpoint commands.
